newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut state workers face layoffs - report.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut state workers face layoffs - report.

text.p: Gov. John Rowland's budget chief has told the heads of 40 state agencies that they should lay off workers if early retirement goals are not met, the Hartford Courant reported Thursday.

Budget Chief Michael Kozlowski outlined cost-reduction goals of the state's early retirement program, and said state agencies would have to meet stiff employee-reduction quotas through either retirement or layoffs.
The Rowland administration wants to save $200 million over two years through early retirement.
The administration now projects that in order to save the money, some 50 percent or more of eligible workers at many agencies should take advantage of the early-retirement program by Aug. 1.
Rowland's office thinks it is crucial to maintain a free hand to lay off people if necessary, the Courant said.
It said that despite recent statements by Rowland, layoffs are now contemplated even without a declaration of a financial emergency.
